title: Matched mirror bank (current-steering unit)
description: A bank of identical unit current sources, the building block of a current-steering DAC or a binary/thermometer bias array. One diode-connected unit device sets the reference; the bank is $N_{legs}$ copies of it, sized width-first as unit-device multiples (bank width = $N_{legs}$ times the unit), so every element is a faithful replica and the full-scale current is $N_{legs}$ times the unit current, give or take the channel-length-modulation gain error between the reference diode point and the shared output rail. Matching is what limits a current-steering converter's linearity: each unit element has a Pelgrom current spread, and across $N_{legs}$ elements the worst-case accumulated error grows as the square root of $N$ (a random-walk bound), which is the estimate this sheet reports and budgets. Compliance is a single saturation voltage, since the bank shares one output rail; a cascoded bank (see the cascode mirror) would trade headroom for a flatter output. The unit reference is diode-connected, so its drop is read off the table rather than estimated.

params.note: DC level of the shared output rail

params.name: L
params.note: longer L lowers the gain error and adds matching area

params.name: gm_id_m
params.note: unit-element inversion: lower gm/ID (higher V*) tightens matching but costs compliance headroom

params.name: match_target
params.note: worst-case accumulated 1-sigma matching budget across the bank

doc.title: Unit reference device (diode)
doc.description: The diode-connected unit element at the unit current. Every leg of the bank is a width replica of it, so its Pelgrom current spread is the per-leg matching, and its width sets the bank width.

rows.name: I_fs
rows.note: full-scale bank current at the sized width

rows.name: gain_err
rows.note: systematic full-scale gain error: the lambda mismatch between the reference diode point and the shared output rail

rows.name: sigma_bank
rows.note: worst-case accumulated matching across N_legs unit elements (a square-root-of-N random-walk bound); estimate

rules.note: every unit element saturated at the shared output rail
worst-case accumulated element spread must stay within the linearity budget
